# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Mute to obtain the manual’s rule and relay the Deaf’s visual observations. I will use only symbols from the allowed gesture alphabet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me its exact disarm rule. Ask the Deaf to report the display, light, and each wire's visible colour or marking, then relay that information to me in your next turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads zero. The indicator light is red. Wire one is red, wire two is yellow, and wire three is green.

The Deaf has reported: display zero, red indicator, and wires red, yellow, green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I must not cut a wire yet. I will ask the Mute to provide the relevant instruction and confirm whether the display or indicator changes the choice.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's report: display zero, indicator red, wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three green. What exact manual rule applies, and which wire must I cut?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visual changes: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

The visual information is unchanged, but the manual’s instruction has still not reached me. Since cutting without that rule would risk immediate detonation, I will wait for the Mute to relay it.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. I decode Mute's Morse gestures as RED WIN ON KIA ON, but it is incoherent and not safe to act on.

The Deaf’s report indicates that the Mute attempted to communicate by gestures, but the decoded message is not reliable. I will establish an unambiguous code: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory sign means wire 2, and the three-finger sign means wire 3. The Mute should send exactly the selected wire’s symbol, and the Deaf should report the symbol rather than interpret it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact code to identify the wire required by the manual: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Gesture exactly one of those symbols to the Deaf, with no other symbols. The Deaf must report the exact symbol.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest Morse decodes literally as RWIE RWI ON, which is unclear and not safe to treat as an instruction. Do not act yet.

The manual instruction is still unavailable, and the reported Morse decoding is ambiguous. No wire is safe to cut. I will ask the Deaf to identify the Mute’s next gesture by its literal hand symbol, while asking the Mute to send one unambiguous wire symbol only.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use Morse or encode letters. Send exactly one gesture: 👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Send nothing else.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please report the next hand gesture literally as one of these: thumbs-up, victory sign, or three-finger sign. Do not decode it as Morse.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent only one Morse dot, decoding as E; no actionable instruction yet. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.

The manual rule and the required wire are still unknown. The Mute’s Morse-like signal cannot safely identify a wire, so I will send the agreed three-symbol wire code directly as a visual reminder and make no cut.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent only Morse E; there is still no actionable instruction. Do not manipulate the bomb.

The manual’s required wire remains unknown, and the bomb must not be manipulated based on Morse guesses. I will send the Mute a single, explicit visual request to answer with one wire symbol only; I will continue waiting rather than cut.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "👍", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new instruction: Mute again sent only E. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Do not act.

The Mute still has not conveyed the manual’s rule, and the only reported signal is an ambiguous Morse “E.” I will not infer a wire from that. I am asking for a visibly distinct three-symbol answer, with one symbol corresponding to each wire, rather than Morse.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "👌", "👍", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```
